clauses.reason: This clause inserts the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business into the membership list in section 305 of Executive Order No. 10973, which establishes the Development Loan Committee. It ends when the parent order's section 305 ends. Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673) revokes "Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;" in section 1-903(a)(1), and section 1-905 makes the order effective "as of" October 1, 1979 (the text prints "October 1,1979."). Section 1-505 of the same order re-establishes a Development Loan Committee "in accordance with section 122(e)" and gives it a new member list that names "the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Industry" and Trade, not the office inserted by this order. The strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 makes the insertion continue until the parent ends, and the replacement list shows why the revocation extinguished this command rather than being a bare cleanup. First end 1979-10-01, read inclusively (the clause was last in force on September 30, 1979). No earlier end is shown (see the order-level checks).

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11417.txt; 33 FR 10625, PDF page 5 of the issue of Friday, July 26, 1968) is Executive Order 11417, whose printed heading adds an Assistant Secretary of Commerce to the membership of the Development Loan Committee. The held text prints the signing date only as "July 1968."; the census register row gives 1968-07-24, and the same page carries a Federal Register filing line dated July 25, 1968. Inventory: the order is one operative paragraph, and it is the whole order. It further amends Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3, 1961, as amended, by inserting in section 305, after the Assistant Secretary of the Treasury dealing with international finance, the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business. The held text of Executive Order 10973 (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_10973.txt) shows that section 305 establishes the Development Loan Committee and lists its members. The text that follows the order on the held PDF pages (Commerce regulations at 33 FR 10627) belongs to other documents. End: Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12163.txt) provides in section 1-903(a)(1) that "Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;" is revoked, and in section 1-905 that "The provisions of this order shall become effective as of" October 1, 1979 (the text then reads "October 1,1979."). The insertion made by this order exists only as words inside section 305 of the parent order; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the clause therefore continues, amended, until the parent ends. Executive Order 12163 is also not a cleanup revocation. Its section 1-505 re-establishes a Development Loan Committee, stated to be "in accordance with section 122(e)" of the Act, with a new list of members that names the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Trade and does not name the office this order inserted, so from October 1, 1979 the old list in section 305 and the insertion in it have no continuing text. The first end is recorded as the effective date, October 1, 1979; the clause was last in force on September 30, 1979. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order (jobs/later-events/output/CATALOG_INDEX.csv) reads "Revoked by: EO 12163, September 29, 1979"; it gives the signing date of Executive Order 12163, and the effective date in section 1-905 is October 1, 1979. The catalog note for Executive Order 10973 carries the same revocation by Executive Order 12163. Earlier ends: none shown. This order states no duration of its own. The dossier lists later amenders of the parent: Executive Orders 11579, 11685, 11816, 11841, 11959 and 12118, and the catalog note for the parent also lists Executive Orders 11261, 11432 and 12107 as amending it. I searched the held text of each for the number 305, for the word Loan and for the word Committee. Executive Orders 11261 (section 304), 11432 (section 301), 11579, 11685, 11816, 11959 and 12118 contain no occurrence; Executive Order 12107 mentions only a list of orders in which the Civil Service Commission is replaced and does not mention section 305; Executive Order 11841 (held only as an American Presidency Project text, which I do not cite) adds a new section 306 for a Development Coordination Committee and does not mention section 305. A Cruden search of the held order texts for the phrase Development Loan Committee finds it only in Executive Orders 10742, 10973, 11417 and 12163 and in the Statutes at Large text of section 204 of the Foreign Assistance Act (75 Stat. 424). I also searched the held text of Public Law 93-189 (87 Stat. 714) for the words Development Loan and Loan Com and found no hit. No held source shows that the Committee or the order's insertion ended before October 1, 1979. Not claimed: whether the Committee continued to meet or to rest on section 204 or section 122(e) of the Foreign Assistance Act between 1973 and 1979 is not shown by a held statute text; the claim rests on the express text of section 305 as amended, which stood until revoked. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes), chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning, with the by-number and phrase scans above. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12163 section 1-904 begins "Except to the extent inconsistent with this order, all" delegations, determinations and other actions made before the order and not revoked continue in force until amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority; this saves completed actions, not the old section 305 membership list. Membership of the Development Loan Committee moves to the new list in section 1-505 of Executive Order 12163, so the effect transfers to that provision.
